scopeMarkdown:
Build **rayx 1.0.0**, the new RayX command-line tool for Native Shell (NSH) apps, in this repository, as the
accepted design `docs/architecture/rayx-nsh-proposal.md` (revision 4, decisions D1 to D15) describes. That document is
the authority for intent; this epic turns it into criteria and work.

## In scope

- **The repository:** the Cargo package `rayx-cli` (library `rayx_cli`, binary `rayx`), version 1.0.0, its CI,
  cargo-dist and release-plz configuration, repository guards and AgentX memory.
- **The machine side, ported from `RayX.CLI.Old` @ `d006250`** (D13): the host layer, the setup engine with its
  records, project discovery and pins, the base and optional sets adapted for NSH (§6, D3, D15), the WSL and Lima
  guests with refresh, migration and removal, `doctor`, `self update` and `fmt`. The GPUI app pipeline (`src/app/`
  except the prerequisite logic) and the GPU set are not ported.
- **Managing nsh** (D1, D2, D10, D11, D7): the pin from `Cargo.lock` or `rayx.toml`, the store under
  `$RAYX_HOME/nsh`, installing from a release archive or from source, `rayx nsh status|path|install|prune`, the
  base-set `nsh` step and doctor's nsh lines.
- **Running nsh** (D12): `rayx app`, the prerequisite map, `RAYX_NSH` and path checkouts, `rayx new` with nsh's own
  templates (D5), `rayx serve`.
- **Fork releases** (D6, D8, D9): the fork-only `fork/release` branch with `.github/workflows/fork-release.yml`, and
  the fork docs on `private/fork-docs`.
- **Proof:** real installs, an app made by `rayx new` on the web, macOS and the iOS simulator, and Gamify (read only).
- **Owner-run release:** the fork's first release (`fork-0.2.0-4`), Linux and Windows verification, the old README's
  links, the new GitHub repository and the 1.0.0 release.

## Out of scope

- Gamify's move to rayx (its `xtask`, Playwright support, README and quality stages, design §9): a follow-up epic in
  Gamify once rayx 1.0.0 is released. This epic only proves rayx against Gamify without changing it.
- App templates for `rayx new` beyond nsh's three (D5).
- Intel Macs get no fork archive and install from source; Windows ARM64 archives come once NSH builds there (D8).
- Threaded web (D3).

## Assumptions and environment

- The development machine is an Apple silicon Mac with Xcode, an iOS simulator runtime, Homebrew (with `llvm`), Rust
  1.99.0, Node 20+ and pnpm, Lima, and `gh` authenticated as `dXnSix` with push rights to `dXnSix/nsh` and
  `rayx-ui`.
- The fork worktrees `../../dXn/nsh/nsh-wt/release` (branch `fork/release`, from `origin/main` at `327bb9e`) and
  `../../dXn/nsh/nsh-wt/fork-docs` (branch `private/fork-docs`) exist; they were created when this epic was planned.
- Real proofs need the network (GitHub, crates.io, npm for `nsh check`) and take minutes: the first NSH source
  build is about four minutes.
- Pushing, opening or merging pull requests, dispatching workflows, creating the GitHub repository, setting secrets
  and releasing need the owner's go-ahead at that moment; the owner-run sprint holds all of them.
constraintsMarkdown:
- The design's decisions D1 to D15 hold. Where this epic adds detail (the default pin's crate list, the archive
  platform names, the Windows ARM64 matrix entry), the design records it as a decision here.
- `AGENTS.md` rules hold: one package with a thin binary; public dependencies only (`tests/dependency_sources.rs`);
  rayx names NSH and nothing above it, and depends on no NSH crate (`tests/library_guard.rs`); no
  `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")` outside tests; every external program through `host::Runner`; no password or token is
  read, stored or forwarded; no self-elevation; licenses only with `--yes`; `--check` executes, installs, records
  and downloads nothing.
- rayx never runs the `nsh` on `PATH`; it runs the build of the pin, in the directory it read the pin in, without
  `CARGO` in the environment.
- Ported behaviour stays as in rayx 1.4.1 unless a criterion here changes it. Records keep their locations
  (`~/.config/rayx/setup.json`, `guests.json`; `%LOCALAPPDATA%\rayx` on Windows) and schema version 1.
- Fork work follows the fork's rules: no AgentX, RayX or Gamify files in the fork, no push to `upstream`, no `v*`
  tag. `fork/release` changes nothing but `.github/workflows/fork-release.yml`; upstream's workflows stay untouched.
- Gamify and `RayX.CLI.Old` are not changed, except `RayX.CLI.Old`'s README install links in the owner-run sprint.
- Diagnostics never contain tokens, environment values or secrets; raw output goes to ignored
  `artifacts-temp/agentx/rayx-1-0/`.

requirements.title: Repository foundation
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: The package, its guards, CI, release configuration and AgentX memory.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
One Cargo package `rayx-cli` at the root: version `1.0.0`, edition 2024, `license = "Apache-2.0"`, `repository = "https://github.com/rayx-ui/RayX.CLI"`, `publish = false`, library `rayx_cli` (`src/lib.rs`) and a thin binary `rayx` (`src/main.rs`); `rust-toolchain.toml` pins `1.99.0` with `clippy` and `rustfmt`. `rayx --version` prints `rayx 1.0.0`. `rayx --help` lists exactly `setup`, `doctor`, `wsl`, `lima`, `self`, `fmt`, `app`, `nsh`, `new` and `serve`; an unknown command or flag exits 2 with clap's usage.

Verified by the new groups `tests/package_layout.rs` and `tests/cli_surface.rs`.

Repository guards. `tests/dependency_sources.rs` (ported) accepts only crates.io and `https` git dependencies pinned to a `rev`, with no `path`, `branch`, `tag` or `[replace]`. `tests/library_guard.rs` (new, D14) fails when `Cargo.toml` or `Cargo.lock` names a RayX, gpux, GPUI or NSH crate (`rayx_app*`, `rayx_runtime`, `rayx`, `gpux*`, `gpui*`, `nsh-*`), when non-test `src/` names `rayx_app`, `gpux`, `GameX` or `Gamify`, or uses `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")`; its allowlist (such as nsh's `gpui` target name in the prerequisite map) fails when an entry no longer matches.

Verified by both groups, each with a failing fixture per rule.

CI: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on pull requests and pushes to `main` in `rayx-ui/RayX.CLI` only: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` (ignored proofs excluded) on `ubuntu-24.04`, `macos-latest` and `windows-latest`. `release-plz.yml` (release pull request and tag on pushes to `main`, `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN`) and cargo-dist's `release.yml` (on `v*` tags) are present. No workflow has duplicate keys.

Verified by `tests/release_automation.rs` (ported, adapted) and the workflow YAML check.

Release configuration: `dist-workspace.toml` with cargo-dist's pinned version, the targets `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-apple-darwin`, `aarch64-pc-windows-msvc`, `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`, the shell and PowerShell installers, `install-path = ["$RAYX_HOME/bin", "~/.rayx/bin"]`, sha256 checksums and GitHub attestations; `release-plz.toml` in git-only mode with `v{{ version }}` tags, `release_commits = "^(feat|fix|perf)"`, `git_release_enable = false`, the 1.x policy comment and a changelog header naming `rayx`; `docs/releasing.md` covering the first release (1.0.0), the 1.x policy, the token, the by-hand fallback and checking a release.

Verified by `tests/release_config.rs` and `tests/release_policy.rs` (ported, adapted).

AgentX memory exists: `.agentx/memory/knowledge/INDEX.md` and `.agentx/memory/decisions/INDEX.md`, domains following the CLI's modules (`host`, `project`, `setup`, `nsh`, `app`, `distribution`, `repository`) with `INDEX.md`, `state.md`, `knowledge.md`, `rules.md` and `hypotheses.md` each, AgentX frontmatter on every file and `state.md` backlinks to the source. The decisions of `RayX.CLI.Old` that still hold (one `Runner`; pins from the project or the defaults table; one setup plan for setup, `--check` and doctor; scripts in WSL with `--exec`; Android Studio's own wizard on Windows; named Lima VMs never adopted; the guest layer with records, refresh and side-by-side replacement; release-plz with dist; cargo-dist with axoupdater; one package with public dependencies) are carried over, adapted, each noting where it came from and carrying `agentx.promoted_from: rayx-1-0`; the taxonomy decision is recorded. The AgentX memory audit reports no errors.

Verified by the memory audit check.

requirements.title: The machine side, ported
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Rayx 1.4.1's machine side in the new package (D13), with its behaviour unchanged unless a criterion says otherwise.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
The host layer (`host::{mod, probe, runner, path_env}`: host facts, `Probe`, `Runner` with execute/print/record modes and privileges, user `PATH` and persistent variables) is ported unchanged in behaviour.

Verified by the ported groups `command_runner`, `host_facts` and `path_env`.

The setup engine is ported: `Set`, `Step`, `Probed`, `Install`, `Action`, `plan`/`check`/`execute`/`run_plan`, `--check` (prints, installs and records nothing, exit 1 when something is missing), `--yes`, the outdated-item prompt, and `setup.json` at its 1.x location in schema version 1 with atomic writes.

Verified by the ported groups `setup_engine` and `setup_update_prompt`.

Project discovery and pins: `Project::discover` (Cargo first, the manifest fallback) without the per-package dependency model of the old pipeline; the pins table and resolution of design §7 (`rust_toolchain`, `wasm_bindgen`, `node`, `jdk`, `android_platform` default `android-35`, `android_build_tools` default `35.0.1`, `android_ndk`, `android_system_image`, `xcode`, `ubuntu`; no `web_toolchain`, `playwright` or `android_ndk_api`), each with its source; `[workspace.metadata.rayx] tools-node`; `rayx fmt [--check]` ported.

Verified by the ported groups `project_pins`, `pin_sources` and `fmt_command`.

The guests are ported: the shared guest layer, `setup --wsl` and `rayx wsl status|compact|remove`, `setup --lima` with sizing, edits and named VMs, `rayx lima remove`, `guests.json`, `setup --update [--vm]` with the refresh, chosen releases, side-by-side Ubuntu migration and removal. Changes: `--wsl` runs no Windows-side GPU step; `wsl compact --clean` also removes `.nsh/`; recorded guest flags never contain `--gpu` (an old record's `--gpu` is dropped on the next write); guests install rayx from `rayx-ui/RayX.CLI` releases.

Verified by the ported groups `guest_layer`, `guest_migration`, `guest_records`, `guest_refresh`, `guest_release`, `guest_remove`, `guest_repairs_flow`, `guest_repairs_safety`, `lima_named_vms`, `setup_lima`, `setup_lima_edit`, `setup_lima_sizing`, `setup_update`, `update_target_vm`, `wsl_disk`, `wsl_install` and `wsl_plan`.

`rayx doctor [--json]` is ported: every applicable set's steps with status, found version and exact fix, the pins with their sources, guests, the interactive desktop and the WSL findings; it has no GPU section and exits 0 whenever the host could be inspected.

Verified by the ported group `doctor`, which also takes the old `pin_sources` test `doctor_shows_only_project_and_default_sources` (doctor's pins show only the `project` and `default` sources), adapted to `android-36`.

`rayx self update [--check] [--release X.Y.Z] [--yes]` is ported: axoupdater for app `rayx-cli` from `rayx-ui/RayX.CLI`, the install-source classification, release existence probes, the downgrade confirmation and the refresh offer; `1.0.0` is the oldest release that can be named and every release offers the refresh.

Verified by the ported groups `self_update`, `self_update_refresh`, `self_update_release`, `release_module` and `release_probe`.

No GPU set and no GPUI pipeline (D15, D13): `Set` has `base`, `web`, `test`, `ios` and `android`; `rayx setup --gpu` is rejected as an unknown argument (exit 2); `--all` selects the applicable sets of that list; the source has no `setup::gpu` and no `app` pipeline modules.

Verified by tests in `setup_engine`.

requirements.title: Setup sets for NSH
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: The sets install what NSH needs (design §6, D3, D15).

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
Base set on macOS (Command Line Tools, Homebrew, rustup, the project toolchain, `~/.cargo/bin` on `PATH`) as in 1.x. On Linux, one apt batch of NSH's packages: `build-essential`, `pkg-config`, `git`, `curl`, `clang`, `llvm`, `libclang-dev`, `libgtk-4-dev`, `libwebkitgtk-6.0-dev` and GStreamer's base and good plugins, with none of gpux's X11, Wayland or Vulkan libraries; a distribution older than Ubuntu 24.04 or Debian 13 is refused with a message naming GTK 4.14 and WebKitGTK 6.0.

Verified by `setup_macos` (ported) and `setup_linux` (rewritten).

Base set on Windows: winget, Build Tools (with the ARM64 component on ARM64), the VC++ redistributable, LLVM and its `PATH`, rustup with the native default host, as in 1.x, without the `fxc.exe` step; a WebView2 Runtime probe, installed with `winget install Microsoft.EdgeWebView2Runtime` when missing.

Verified by `setup_windows` (ported, adapted).

`--web`: `wasm32-unknown-unknown` on the project toolchain; `wasm-bindgen-cli` at `Cargo.lock`'s `wasm-bindgen` version only when the lock has one; Homebrew's `llvm` on macOS. No nightly toolchain and no `rust-src` (D3).

Verified by `setup_web` (rewritten).

`--test` as in 1.x (Node at the pin, pnpm through corepack, xvfb and Playwright's libraries on Linux, the project's Playwright package from `tools-node` and its Chromium); `setup::test_tools` exposes the installed Playwright Chromium's executable path for `rayx app test --target web`.

Verified by `setup_test_tools` and `setup_node_selection` (ported).

`--ios`: Xcode (mas or xcodes), `xcode-select`, the license, first launch, the iOS simulator runtime, and the targets `aarch64-apple-ios`, `aarch64-apple-ios-sim` and `aarch64-apple-ios-macabi` on the project toolchain; no XcodeGen.

Verified by `setup_ios` (ported, adapted).

`--android`: the JDK at the pin, `JAVA_HOME`, Android Studio (optional for builds), the SDK command-line tools, `platform-tools`, `platforms;android-35`, `build-tools;35.0.1`, the NDK at the pin, the emulator and its system image, a default AVD, acceleration, and the targets `aarch64-linux-android`, `armv7-linux-androideabi` and `x86_64-linux-android`; no `cargo-ndk`. The NDK is found the way nsh finds it: `ANDROID_NDK_HOME` (the one variable nsh reads) satisfies the pin when it names a directory and is reported, with its fix, when it names none; `ANDROID_NDK_ROOT` and `NDK_HOME` choose nothing.

Verified by `setup_android` and `setup_android_pins` (ported, adapted).

requirements.title: Fork releases
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Every `fork-*` tag of `dXnSix/nsh` gets a release with NSH's compiled distribution per platform (D6, D8, D9).

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
On the fork branch `fork/release`, `.github/workflows/fork-release.yml` is the only change from `origin/main`. It runs on pushed `fork-*` tags and by hand with a `tag` input; checks that the tag is `fork-<workspace version>-<n>` and that its commit is on `origin/main`; builds the distribution with upstream's `dist` job steps (Java 17, Android 35, stable Rust with wasm32, LLVM, GTK 4 on Linux, `cargo xtask dist -v`, the smoke test) for `macos-arm64` (`macos-15`), `linux-x86_64` (`ubuntu-24.04`), `linux-arm64` (`ubuntu-24.04-arm`) and `windows-x86_64` (`windows-latest`), plus `windows-arm64` (`windows-11-arm`), which may fail without blocking the release; the `linux-arm64` archive has no Android runtime, because the Android NDK has no toolchain for arm64 Linux: that leg skips the Android SDK and switches the Android part of `cargo xtask dist` off in its own checkout, stopping the run when NSH's code no longer matches; a Windows runner without an Android SDK builds without the runtime, as `xtask dist` allows; packs `nsh-<platform>.tar.gz` (`.zip` on Windows) holding `nsh/`, each with a `.sha256`, and attests them; then publishes (never a draft) a release named after the tag with generated notes and those assets, once the four required platforms built. It attaches no installers and touches no Homebrew, Scoop or crates.io.

Verified statically (no duplicate keys; the triggers and the required `tag` input, exactly the five platforms, `windows-arm64` alone non-blocking, `linux-arm64` alone without Android, the archive check naming exactly the required platforms' archives, a non-draft release named after the tag with generated notes, the attestation, and no installers, asserted from the parsed YAML); its run is proven by OWN-2.

The fork docs on `private/fork-docs`: the README describes `fork/*` branches (fork-only changes that never go upstream and get no draft in `prs/`), says a `fork-*` tag now produces a release through `fork-release.yml` (about an hour; four required platforms, Windows ARM64 when it builds) and says how consumers move to a new tag: the pins in `src/frontend/.cargo/config.toml` and the places `cargo xtask nsh verify` names, the `cargo install` of the CLI while a consumer does not run NSH through rayx, and `rayx setup` once it does. `scripts/sync-main.sh upstream`, and `branch` for a topic branch, warn, naming `.github/workflows/release.yml` and `fork-release.yml`, when the merged upstream range changes `.github/workflows/release.yml`, and print nothing about it otherwise.

Verified by the new TAP script `scripts/tests/sync-main-release-warning.sh` (throwaway repositories: `upstream` with and without a change, and `branch` with one).

requirements.title: The nsh pin
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Which nsh a project uses (design §4.1, D10, D7).

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
The pin is read from the workspace's `Cargo.lock`: every NSH package (the crates of the defaults table's list, and `nsh-platform-gpui` from NSH's `crates/gpui`, as nsh's own list has them; an app's own `nsh-app-*` crates are not NSH's) must have one source; `git+…?tag=…#<commit>` gives a git pin with id = the commit's first 12 hex digits; `?branch=`/`?rev=` and other git URLs give a git pin with no release (the ref decoded from Cargo's percent-encoding); a crates.io source gives an upstream release pin `v<version>`; no source gives a path pin to the NSH checkout containing the crate. The workspace is found from the current directory (or `-C`) with `cargo locate-project`, else from the manifests when cargo cannot run (a fresh machine, a missing toolchain); outside any workspace, from the crates `nsh.json` lists under `"rust"`. A missing lock is written by `cargo metadata` first when the command executes (`rayx setup`, `rayx app`, `rayx nsh path|install`); a dry run (`--check`, `doctor`, `rayx nsh status`, the project reads of `rayx nsh prune`) writes nothing and reports the pin as unknown until the lock exists. A workspace with neither a lock nor a working cargo is an error, never the default. Two sources stop with both named.

Verified by the new group `tests/nsh_pin.rs`, with fixture locks including Gamify's shape.

With no NSH crates, the pin is the `[nsh]` table of `rayx.toml` beside `nsh.json` (`git`, `tag`, `commit`, or `version` for an upstream release); a tag whose commit differs from the recorded one is an error. NSH crates and an `[nsh]` table together stop with both named. With neither, rayx uses the built-in default and, inside an app, warns on every command, showing the three lines that pin it.

Verified by `tests/nsh_pin.rs`.

The defaults table holds the default pin (`https://github.com/dXnSix/nsh`, `fork-0.2.0-4`, `327bb9ea65d08ffac4af498cc7fbbfa18a1b3623`) and its NSH crate list (the `crates/nsh-*` of that commit). Outside any app the default is used and reported as `default`.

Verified by `tests/nsh_pin.rs`; the crate list is compared with the fork at that commit by `proof_nsh_install`.

Entries live in `$RAYX_HOME/nsh/<id>/`, else `~/.rayx/nsh/<id>/`. `receipt.json` (`version` 1, `id`, `kind` `distribution` or `source`, `url`, `ref`, `commit`, `nsh`, `cli`, `installed`) is written last; an entry without it is unfinished, and the next install resumes it (a source entry reuses its checkout and target directory; a distribution is downloaded again). An install holds `<id>.lock`; a second rayx waits, says so, and then finds the entry installed. A complete entry whose CLI no longer answers as the pin wants loses its receipt before it is installed again, so an interrupted repair leaves it unfinished. A dry run writes nothing, not even the lock. Nothing is written outside the store and the system temporary directory.

Verified by the new group `tests/nsh_store.rs`.

`rayx nsh prune [--yes]` lists the entries that no recorded project (`setup.json` roots, each project's pin) and not the default pins, with their sizes, and removes them after a `[y/N]`; `--yes` removes without asking; without a terminal and without `--yes` nothing is removed and it exits 1. An entry another rayx is installing (its lock held) is kept, and lock files stay; while a recorded project's pin cannot be read, nothing is pruned and the reason is shown. `rayx setup --update` offers the same after its runs, except with `--check` or `--vm`.

Verified by `tests/nsh_store.rs`.

requirements.title: Installing nsh
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: From a release archive first, from source as the fallback (design §4.3, D11).

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
From a release: the host's platform name (`macos-arm64`, `linux-x86_64`, `linux-arm64`, `windows-x86_64`, `windows-arm64`; none on other hosts), `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/<tag>/nsh-<platform>.tar.gz` (`.zip` on Windows) and its `.sha256`, the digest checked (a mismatch installs nothing and names both digests), `nsh/` unpacked into `<id>/nsh/`, the CLI checked, a `distribution` receipt. Fork pins use the pin's repository and tag; crates.io pins use `longbridge/nsh` at `v<version>`. A missing archive falls back to source with a line naming the archive it missed.

Verified by the new group `tests/nsh_install.rs` (recorded `Runner` and local archive fixtures).

From source: `git init`, `git fetch --depth 1 <url> <commit>` (falling back to fetching the ref when the host refuses a commit), a detached checkout in `<id>/source/`, `core.longPaths true` on Windows, `rustup toolchain install` in the checkout, then `cargo build --release --locked -p nsh-cli --target-dir target` there (the target directory pinned inside the entry, whatever `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` or `build.target-dir` say), both without `CARGO` and `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN` (so NSH's own `rust-toolchain.toml` applies) and run as the Rust steps find them (on `PATH`, else in `~/.cargo/bin`, as in the same `rayx setup` run that installed rustup); a `source` receipt. The CLI check (both paths): `nsh --version` must name the lock's NSH version and the pin's commit, else nothing is recorded and the error names both.

Verified by `tests/nsh_install.rs`.

Real installs on this Mac into a temporary `RAYX_HOME`: upstream `v0.2.0` from its release (the `macos-arm64` archive) prints `nsh 0.2.0`; `fork-0.2.0-4` from source prints `nsh 0.2.0 (327bb9e)`; installing either again changes nothing; the default pin's crate list equals the `crates/nsh-*` of the fork at `327bb9e`.

Verified by the ignored group `tests/proof_nsh_install.rs`.

requirements.title: rayx nsh, the setup step and doctor
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Managing the store from the command line and through setup (design §4.5).

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`rayx nsh status [--json]` shows the pin (ref and short commit, or version), its source (`project`, `rayx.toml` or `default`), the id, the kind, whether it is installed, its size and the CLI's path. `rayx nsh path` prints the CLI's path, installing it first; with `--no-install` a missing entry exits 1 with the `rayx setup` command. `rayx nsh install` installs the pin.

Verified by the new group `tests/nsh_command.rs`.

The base set ends with an `nsh` step after the project's toolchain: its probe is the receipt plus `nsh --version`, its install §4.3; it asks nothing; `--check` prints its commands and installs nothing. A pin that cannot be read (two sources, a broken `rayx.toml`, no lock yet in a dry run) fails the step with the reason (the step reads the pin again when it runs, so a fresh machine's first `rayx setup` installs the project's pin once Rust is in place); the built-in default never stands in, and doctor shows the reason. `rayx setup` records a Cargo workspace by its root and an app without one by its directory; `rayx setup --update` installs each recorded project's pin. `rayx doctor` shows one line per pin (`nsh  fork-0.2.0-4 (327bb9e)  project  installed  <size>`), and `--json` has the same fields.

Verified by the new group `tests/setup_nsh.rs`.

requirements.title: Running nsh
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: `rayx app` and how it reaches nsh (design §4.4, §4.6, §6.1, D12).

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`rayx app [-C <dir>] [--no-install] <command> [arguments]` runs the pin's CLI with every argument after the command unchanged (including `--` and what follows), in the current directory or `-C`, which is also where the pin was read. The environment loses `CARGO`; `CC_wasm32_unknown_unknown` and `AR_wasm32_unknown_unknown` are set to the web set's LLVM only when unset; `ANDROID_NDK_HOME` is set to the pinned NDK in the SDK only when it is unset and that NDK is installed (nsh otherwise builds with the newest NDK of the SDK); everything else passes through. On Unix rayx replaces itself with nsh; on Windows it ignores Ctrl+C (which reaches nsh in the same console), waits and exits with nsh's code.

Verified by the new group `tests/nsh_run.rs`.

The prerequisite step maps the command and `--target` to sets as design §6.1 says (web for `--target web`; web and test for `test --target web`; ios for `ios`, `ios-simulator`, `catalyst`; android for `android`; none for desktop targets and for `build`, `check`, `init`, `keygen`, `certify`, `publish`, `verify`, `revoke`, `symbolicate`). Missing steps that need no administrator rights or license answer, the pinned nsh among them, are installed with a line saying so; others are asked about in a terminal or refused with the exact `rayx setup` command; `--no-install` reports instead. On a host `rayx setup` does not support, the other sets are not checked, but the pinned nsh still is, with `rayx nsh install -C <dir>` as its command. `test --target web` without `--browser`, on a host with no Chrome, Edge or Chromium, gets `--browser <the test set's Chromium>`.

Verified by the new group `tests/app_prereqs.rs`.

`RAYX_NSH=<path>` runs that binary instead of resolving and installing a pin, with `rayx: RAYX_NSH=<path> replaces the project's nsh <id>` on stderr for every command; a relative path is read against the directory rayx started in (never `-C`, never a `PATH` search), and `rayx nsh path` prints it, with the same warning. A path pin builds `cargo build --release -p nsh-cli --target-dir target` in that checkout and runs its `target/release/nsh`, writing nothing to the store.

Verified by the new group `tests/nsh_fork_dev.rs`.

requirements.title: rayx new
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: A new app pinned from its first commit (design §4.7, D5, D7).

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`rayx new <dir> [--name <name>] [--template mixed|ts|rust]` (default `mixed`) installs the default pin if needed and runs its `nsh init <dir>` with the name and template. For `mixed` and `rust` it writes `.cargo/config.toml` with a `[patch.crates-io]` entry for every crate of the default pin's crate list (git URL and tag) and runs `cargo generate-lockfile`, after which the app's pin is the default; for `ts` it writes `rayx.toml` with the default's `[nsh]` table. It prints the next steps (`rayx setup --web`, `--ios` on a Mac, `rayx app run`). A directory nsh refuses (existing files) is left unchanged, and so is one that already has the file rayx would write (`.cargo/config.toml`, or `rayx.toml` for `ts`): `rayx new` refuses before anything runs; an unknown template is rejected listing the three.

Verified by the new group `tests/new_app.rs`.

requirements.title: rayx serve
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: A static host for what `nsh package --target web` writes (design §5).

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`rayx serve [--dir <site>] [--port <port>]` listens on `127.0.0.1` at `--port`, else `PORT`, else 8080, serving `--dir` (default the current directory): files with their MIME types (`.wasm` as `application/wasm`, `.js` as `text/javascript`, HTML, CSS, JSON, images, fonts), `index.html` for a directory, `GET /health` answering 200, and 404 for anything outside the site (`..`, encoded or not); responses carry `Cache-Control: no-store`.

Verified by the new group `tests/serve.rs` against a running server.

requirements.title: Real proof
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: rayx with real NSH, real apps and Gamify, on this Mac.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
With a temporary `RAYX_HOME`, an app made by `rayx new` (`mixed`) builds (`rayx app build`), runs on the web (`rayx app run --target web --strict-port --port

` answers `/nsh.version`), passes `rayx app test --target web`, and its `rayx app package --target web --out

` output served by `rayx serve` answers `/health` and `index.html`. Verified by the ignored group `tests/proof_app_web.rs`.

The same app passes `rayx app test --target macos` and `rayx app test --target ios` on the iOS simulator.

Verified by the ignored group `tests/proof_app_apple.rs`.

In Gamify's `src/frontend` (`RAYX_PROOF_GAMIFY`, default `../../Six/Six.Gamify/src/frontend`): `rayx nsh status` shows `fork-0.2.0-4 (327bb9e)` from `project`; `rayx app check .` passes; `rayx app package . --target web --out <tmp>` succeeds and `rayx serve --dir <tmp>/Gamify` answers `/health` and serves the page and its `.wasm` as `application/wasm`; Gamify's tracked files are unchanged afterwards. It needs Gamify's `config/runtime.json` (from its `cargo xtask config`).

Verified by the ignored group `tests/proof_gamify.rs`.

requirements.title: Documentation
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: The README and the project contract.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`README.md`: installing; that this is a new CLI, how it relates to the old one (GPUI apps stay on `RayX.CLI.Old`; the installer replaces the old binary; records and guests carry over); every command with its options; how rayx chooses and installs nsh (pins, `rayx.toml`, the store, prune, `RAYX_NSH`, path checkouts); the sets per target. `docs/projects.md`: the project contract (pins and their sources, `[workspace.metadata.rayx]` keys, `rayx.toml`). `docs/manual-verification.md` with sections for Linux, Windows and WSL, and releases.

Verified by `readme_versions` and `readme_guests` (ported, adapted) and the new `readme_nsh` (every documented command line and every flag of the flag tables exists in the CLI, and every command and flag of the CLI is documented; the sets-per-target table equals the prerequisite map; the documented pins tables of the README and `docs/projects.md` equal the defaults table).

requirements.title: Owner-run release
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Steps that need the owner's go-ahead, accounts or hardware.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown: With the owner's go-ahead: `fork/release` is pushed, its pull request into the fork's `main` passes the fork's CI and is merged with a merge commit; `private/fork-docs` is pushed.

With the owner's go-ahead, `fork-release.yml` run by hand for `fork-0.2.0-4` publishes the release `fork-0.2.0-4` with the four required archives and their digests (and `windows-arm64` if it built); the `macos-arm64` archive prints `nsh 0.2.0 (327bb9e)` on this Mac, and `rayx nsh install` in Gamify's `src/frontend` creates a `distribution` entry.

In a Lima guest on this Mac (`rayx setup --lima --web --test`, plus Playwright's Chromium in the guest, not the Chromium snap, with an AppArmor profile that lets it create its sandbox) and on the owner's Windows PC with WSL (`rayx setup --web --test --yes` first, and Playwright's Chromium in the distribution): `rayx setup --web --test --check`, `rayx doctor` and the web proof pass; results logged in `docs/manual-verification.md`.

With the owner's go-ahead: `RayX.CLI.Old`'s README install links point at `rayx-ui/RayX.CLI.Old` and are pushed before `rayx-ui/RayX.CLI` is created; the repository is created public, `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` is set, the `1.0.0` section of `CHANGELOG.md` is dated, and the first push to `main` makes release-plz tag `v1.0.0` (an initial release, with no release pull request) and cargo-dist publish six targets; the installer over a rayx 1.4.1 install keeps `setup.json` and `guests.json`, and `rayx setup --update` refreshes.
